transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Chen (Redwood); Laura Gomez, Sanjay Rao, Priya Shah (MediconX)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Quick check on onboarding progress; staging VPC pending; some env issues around KMS and SSH.
- Benchmarks: initial run showed P95 spikes at ~480ms on hosted default settings; Ethan suggests tuning batching/kv cache and quantization.
- Action: Redwood to run tuned bench and share pricing/benchmark spreadsheet; customer to grant staging access and provide tokenization sample.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining  quick check, can folks see my screen? (brief pause) cool. quick agenda: onboarding status, access, env readiness, bench results, next steps.
[00:22] Laura (MediconX - CTO): yep see it. we got your note about the p95 spikes, so want to walk through what we saw and what you think.
[00:35] Ethan (Redwood SE): yep, thanks. quick refresher  last week we ran the initial throughput/latency pass on your sample traffic. that was on hosted default settings and we saw average token cost within expected range but p95 latency hits ~450-500ms which is above your target of 200-250.
[00:50] Sanjay (ML Eng): to be clear, that's with our anonymized patient queries, sequence lengths average 512, right? the padding distribution was kinda wide because some queries are 1024.
[01:12] Ethan: correct, padding distribution matters. a couple of things we flagged: batching window, prefix/k-v cache warmup, and quantization profile. with longer tails (1k) you get more kv cache misses.
[01:35] Priya (Infra): on our side, we still need to finish the staging VPC peering and rotate the KMS policy  I submitted a ticket but was waiting for exact CIDR you need.
[01:48] Maya: thanks Priya. that's step one  we need staging peering + bastion details. remind me, you have a strict egress policy and HSM-backed KMS?
[02:00] Priya: yes, must go through our HSM KMS for any model keys, SSO is SAML via Okta, and we need RBAC for audit trails.
[02:12] Maya: got it. we'll provide KMS integration docs (links) and clear instructions for least-priv access. I'll drop the docs link in the follow-up.
[02:25] Laura: about the bench numbers, can you explain 'kv cache warmup'  is that something you can tune from your side or we need to change client traffic?
[02:36] Ethan: good q. KV cache warmup depends on request locality  if you have many unique prefixes it's slower. we can enable prefix caching heuristics and also configure shorter batching thresholds to avoid tail latency. both are runtime config changes we can push in the Dedicated pilot or in a private env.
[02:58] Sanjay: when you say shorter batching thresholds, do you mean drop batch size to prioritize latency? tradeoff with throughput/cost?
[03:10] Ethan: exactly. smaller batches reduces per-request wait time but raises tokens-per-second cost. we can run a multi-config run: low-latency (batch=2, max-wait=10ms), balanced (batch=8), cost-optimized (bigger batches + aggressive kv cache). we'll share the spreadsheet with opt configs.
[03:30] Maya: side note  we noticed you mentioned SOC2 when we kicked off the POC. Priya, do you need the SOC2 and ISO docs?
[03:40] Priya: yes would like SOC2 Type II, encryption in transit at rest, plus audit log retention. also need details on log redaction and where logs live.
[03:52] Maya: we'll send the security pack (redwood_security_summ.pdf) and a short note on audit retention and redaction.
[04:05] Laura: another blocker  our legal team needs clarity on data residency; some PII can't leave eu-west-1. can you do region pinning for the model runtime?
[04:16] Ethan: yes, region pinning is supported; for the POC we can run workloads in the AWS eu-west-1 region. if you want dedicated capacity, we can reserve GPUs there.
[04:27] Sanjay: great. on tokenization  we saw a mismatch in token counts between our tokenizer and the model's default. i'll attach our tokenization samples. can Redwood run the bench using our tokenizer to match effective sequence length?
[04:40] Ethan: absolutely; please upload a small sample (50-100 examples) to the S3 bucket we shared and we'll run the bench with your tokenization. that often explains the p95 delta.
[04:54] Maya: ok action for Sanjay to upload sample. also Ethan will re-run bench with two quant profiles: q4_0 and fp16 and compare p95 + cost.
[05:07] Sanjay: noted. expected timeline?
[05:12] Ethan: i can start runs tomorrow once we have staging peering + token samples. runs take ~6-8 hours to collect stable p95; i'll attach raw logs.
[05:25] Priya: peering  we need an IP range. what do you need from us exactly?
[05:30] Maya: CIDR, bastion host IP (or plan for ssm), and whether you want a service account for KMS integration. i think service account + least privilege is easiest.
[05:40] Priya: ok i'll send CIDR and open the ticket with infra ops.
[05:45] Laura: quick question on fallback strategies  if dedicated is down or overloaded, how do you failover?
[05:52] Ethan: we have smart routing: fallback to hosted model variant or a quantized variant in the same region; you can set a policy to prioritize latency or cost when failing over. we'll show an example config.
[06:06] Sanjay: any chance of using a smaller model for quick answers and large model for long-form? hybrid routing?
[06:14] Ethan: yes  we support tool-calling/rerouting; for instance, short completions to a distilled variant and long responses to the full model. that reduces cost.
[06:26] Maya: circling back timeline: Priya will provide peering details by Friday (6/26). Ethan will run bench and initial tuning and post results by 6/25-6/26. Maya to share pricing + bench spreadsheet by 6/26.
[06:44] Laura: ok good. anything else on infra readiness?
[06:49] Priya: KMS rotation  one ask: can Redwood support HSM key policy for envelope encryption? we don't want keys stored off-prem.
[06:58] Ethan: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM; the runtime doesn't persist plaintext keys and we integrate via envelope encryption. will include technical note.
[07:12] Maya: noted. next big item is security deep-dive with your compliance folks; let's tentatively schedule week of 6/29.
[07:20] Laura: works.
[07:24] (brief cross-talk on calendar invites)
[07:40] Ethan: small note on telemetry  when we share the bench logs we'll include token-level latency, batching stats, kv cache hit-rate, and per-request trace ids for you to map to your logs.
[07:56] Sanjay: perfect. also please include prompt/evauation metrics so we can validate correctness (we saw a small RER earlier).
[08:08] Ethan: yes we'll produce a small eval set and run automatic checks; attach to the bench doc.
[08:16] Maya: ok we'll wrap. recap: Redwood runs tuned bench once peering & tokens arrive; Redwood shares bench + pricing doc; customer provisions peering + KMS info; security deep-dive next week; acceptance criteria to be agreed before pilot end.
[08:35] Laura: thanks everyone.
[08:39] Priya: thanks.
[08:42] Maya: i'll follow up with links and action items in email.

References/Links mentioned:
- Benchmark spreadsheet (shared): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/mediconx-poc (internal link)
- Security pack excerpt: /redwood/security_summ.pdf
- Staging S3 bucket for token samples: s3://redwood-mediconx-samples (access pending)

End of transcript.
